Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 45, verses 1–5:

Tafsir of Surat al-Jathiyah

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

Allah, exalted is He, directs His creation to reflect upon His favors and blessings, and His great power by which He created the heavens and the earth, and what is in them of created beings of differing kinds and types: angels, jinn and humans, animals, birds, wild beasts, predators and insects, and what is in the sea of diverse kinds; and the alternation of night and day, succeeding one another, ceaseless and unending, this one with its darkness and that one with its light; and what Allah, exalted is He, sends down from the clouds as rain at the time of need for it, which He called provision (rizq) because through it provision is obtained. ﴿And with it He gives life to the earth after its death﴾, that is, after it had been barren, with no vegetation in it and nothing at all.

* *

His saying: ﴿and the turning of the winds﴾, that is, south winds and north winds [in Ta and A: "and northern winds"], and east winds and west winds, sea winds and land winds, night winds and day winds. Among them are those that bring rain, among them those that bring fertilization, among them those that are nourishment for spirits, and among them those that are barren [that do not produce] [addition from Ta, M, A].

He first said ﴿for people who believe﴾ [in Ta and A: "for a people who believe," which is an error], then ﴿who are certain﴾, then ﴿who reason﴾, which is an ascent from a noble state to what is nobler and higher than it. These verses resemble the verse in al-Baqarah, which is His saying: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ships that sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what Allah sends down from the sky of water, giving life thereby to the earth after its death, and dispersing therein every kind of moving creature, and the turning of the winds and the clouds controlled between the sky and the earth, are signs for a people who reason﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:164]. Here Ibn Abi Hatim also cited from Wahb ibn Munabbih a long and strange report concerning the creation of man from the four humors.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 45, verses 12–15:

He, exalted is He, mentions His blessings upon His servants in what He has subjected to them of the sea, ﴿so that the ships may sail upon it﴾, meaning the boats (al-sufun) upon it, by His command, for it is He who commanded the sea to carry them. ﴿And that you may seek of His bounty﴾, meaning through trade and earning, ﴿and perhaps you will be grateful﴾, meaning for obtaining the benefits brought to you from distant regions and remote horizons.

Then He said, ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, meaning the stars, the mountains, the seas, the rivers, and everything from which you benefit. That is, all of it is from His bounty, grace and favour; and therefore He said, ﴿all from Him﴾, meaning from Him alone, with no partner in that, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah; then when adversity touches you, to Him you cry for help﴾ [An-Nahl: 53].

Ibn Jarir narrated, through the route of al-'Awfi, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all from Him﴾: "Everything is from Allah, and that 'all' is a name of His names; so ﴿all from Him﴾, and none of the disputants dispute it, and he is certain that it is so."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-'Asqalani narrated to us, al-Firyabi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Abu Arakah, who said: A man asked 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, "Of what was creation created?" He said: "From light and fire, and darkness and dust." He said, "Go to Ibn 'Abbas and ask him." So he went to him and said to him the same, and he said: "Return to him and ask him: of what was all of that created?" So he returned to him and asked him, and he recited: ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all from Him﴾. This is a strange narration, and it contains an objectionable element.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿Say to those who believe: forgive those who do not expect the days of Allah﴾, meaning: they should pardon them and bear the harm from them. This was at the beginning of Islam, when they were commanded to be patient with the harm of the polytheists and the People of the Book, so that this would serve to win their hearts. Then, when they persisted in obstinacy, Allah prescribed for the believers fighting and jihad. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah.

Mujahid said regarding His saying ﴿who do not expect the days of Allah﴾: "They do not care for the blessings of Allah."

* *

His saying: ﴿that He may recompense a people for what they used to earn﴾, meaning: if they pardon them in this world, Allah will requite them for their evil deeds in the Hereafter. Therefore He said: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self, and whoever does evil, it is against it; then to your Lord you will be returned﴾, meaning you will return to Him on the Day of Resurrection, and your deeds will be presented to Him, and He will recompense you for your deeds, good and bad.

His saying ﴿And Allah misled him knowingly﴾ admits of two interpretations:

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 45, verses 27–29:

Allah informs that He is the Owner of the heavens and the earth, the One who judges in them (or: "over them," per one manuscript variant) in this world and the Hereafter. Therefore He said: ﴿And the Day the Hour is established, that Day the falsifiers will be lost.﴾ That is, the Day of Resurrection. ﴿The falsifiers﴾ are those who disbelieve in Allah and deny what He sent down to His messengers of clear signs and manifest proofs.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Sufyan al-Thawri came to Madinah and heard al-Mu'afiri (another manuscript reads "al-'Adari") speaking some of the things with which people laugh. So he said to him: "O shaykh, do you not know that Allah has a Day on which the falsifiers will be lost?" He said: "The effect of this remained visible on al-Mu'afiri until he met Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." Mentioned by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Then He said: ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling﴾. That is, kneeling on their knees out of the severity and greatness (of the situation). It is said that this happens when Hell is brought forward, for it will emit a roar such that no one remains except that he falls to his knees, even Abraham the Friend (Khalil), who will say: "Myself, myself, myself! I ask of You today only for myself." Even Jesus will say: "I ask of You today only for myself; I do not ask You for Mary, who bore me."

Mujahid, Ka'b al-Ahbar and al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿Every nation kneeling﴾ means on their knees. ʿIkrimah said: ﴿Kneeling﴾ means separated, each on its side, not necessarily on the knees. The first view is more preferable.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' related to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah related to us, from 'Amr, from 'Abdullah ibn Babah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is as if I see you kneeling in groups (bi-l-kawam) before Hell." (Abu Nu'aym narrated it in Zawa'id Zuhd Ibn al-Mubarak, no. 360, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (7/299), by way of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah with this chain.)

Isma'il ibn Rafi' al-Madini said, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), in a marfu' narration in the hadith of the Trumpet (al-Sur): "The people will be separated and the nations will kneel, and they are the ones of whom Allah says: ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling; every nation will be called to its record.﴾" (See the explanation of the hadith of the Trumpet at verse 73 of Surah al-An'am.)

This contains a combination of the two views, and there is no contradiction, and Allah knows best.

As for His saying: ﴿Every nation will be called to its record﴾, meaning the record of their deeds, like His saying: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought﴾ [Az-Zumar: 69]. Therefore He said: ﴿Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do﴾, that is, you will be repaid for your deeds, good and bad, like His saying: ﴿On that Day man will be informed of what he sent ahead and kept back. Rather, man, against himself, will be a witness, even if he presents his excuses﴾ [Al-Qiyamah: 13–15].

Then He said: ﴿This, Our Record, speaks against you with truth﴾, that is, it will bring forth all your deeds without any addition or deficiency, like His saying: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say: "Woe to us! What is this Book that leaves nothing small or great but has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present, and your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [Al-Kahf: 49].

He said: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾, meaning: their hearts believed and their limbs performed the righteous deeds [[In manuscripts T and A: "al-salihah"]], which are the sincere deeds that conform to the Shari'ah, ﴿their Lord will admit them to His mercy﴾, which is Paradise, as it is established in the Sahih that Allah said to Paradise: "You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4850), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

﴿That is the clear triumph﴾, meaning: the manifest, evident one.

Then He said: ﴿And as for those who disbelieved: "Were not My verses recited to you? But you were arrogant and were a people committing crimes."﴾ Meaning: it will be said to them as a rebuke and reproach: Were not the verses of the Most Merciful recited to you, but you were arrogant toward following them and turned away when hearing them? ﴿And you were a people committing crimes﴾, meaning: in your deeds, along with what your hearts harbored of denial?

﴿And when it was said, "Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and the Hour, there is no doubt about it"﴾, meaning: when the believers said that to you, ﴿you said, "We do not know what the Hour is."﴾, meaning: we do not recognize it. ﴿We think it is only a assumption﴾, meaning: we only imagine its occurrence as a mere supposition, that is, a weak one [[In A: "marjuw'a" (sic)]]. Therefore He said: ﴿And we are not certain.﴾, meaning: not convinced. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the evil consequences of what they had done became apparent to them﴾, meaning: the punishment for their evil deeds became manifest to them, ﴿and what they had been mocking encompassed them﴾, meaning: it surrounded them, namely the punishment and retribution. ﴿And it will be said, "This Day We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours"﴾, meaning: We will treat you as one who has forgotten you, in the Fire of Hell, ﴿as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours﴾, meaning: you did not work for it because you did not believe in it. ﴿And your refuge is the Fire, and you have no helpers.﴾

It is established in the Sahih that Allah the Exalted says to some of the servants on the Day of Resurrection: "Did I not marry you? Did I not honor you? Did I not subject to you horses and camels, and leave you to lead and to enjoy leadership?" He says: "Yes, O Lord." He says: "Did you think that you would meet Me?" He says: "No." Allah the Exalted says: "Today I forget you as you forgot Me" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2968), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That is because you took the verses of Allah in ridicule﴾, meaning: We only requited you with this recompense because you took the proofs of Allah against you as objects of mockery, scoffing and deriding them. ﴿And the worldly life deceived you﴾, meaning: it deluded you, so you were content with it, and so you became among the losers. Therefore He said: ﴿So today they will not be taken out of it﴾, meaning: out of the Fire, ﴿nor will they be allowed to make amends.﴾, meaning: they will not be asked to make amends; rather they will be punished without reckoning or reproach, just as a group of the believers will enter Paradise without punishment or reckoning.

Then, having mentioned His judgment concerning the believers and the disbelievers, He said: ﴿So all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth﴾, meaning: the Owner of them and whatever is in them. Therefore He said: ﴿Lord of the worlds.﴾

Then He said: ﴿And to Him belongs grandeur in the heavens and the earth﴾. Mujahid said: this means dominion (al-sultan). That is, He is the Mighty, the Glorified, before whom everything is humbled and to whom everything is in need. It has come in the Sahih hadith: "Allah the Exalted says: Majesty is My waist-wrapper and greatness is My cloak; whoever contends with Me over either of them, I will cast into My Fire." Muslim narrated it from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Aghurr Abu Muslim, from Abu Hurairah and Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in similar wording [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2620).]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And He is the Almighty﴾, meaning: the One who cannot be overcome or resisted, ﴿the All-Wise﴾ in His words and deeds, in His legislation and His decree, exalted and sanctified is He; there is no god but Him.

End of the tafsir of Surah al-Jathiyah [And to Allah belong praise and grace].
